trust_decision.summary: Whether a form-submitted username/password pair signs the client in is decided in auth.login via db.verify_user, with no limit on how many failed attempts a client or username may make.

landing_point.why: The advisory names POST /login; this is the only handler for that form and it calls db.verify_user with no attempt counting.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /login via db.verify_user (dummy-hash timing equalisation for unknown users)
aniworld --web-ui -> start_web_ui -> waitress.serve (trusted proxy options so remote_addr is the real client)
new module src/aniworld/web/throttle.py (LoginThrottle), used only by POST /login

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/aniworld/web/app.py:283-285 (waitress.serve called without proxy options; fix.diff:77-103 adds ANIWORLD_WEB_TRUSTED_PROXY so per-IP counting sees the real client behind a reverse proxy)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The server bootstrap and reverse-proxy handling look like deployment configuration rather than the login handler, so a solver keys the throttle on request.remote_addr (or trusts X-Forwarded-For) and never touches start_web_ui.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A correct password must still sign in after a few failures below the limit, a success resets only the username counter (not the IP counter), and lockout of one username must not block other users from other IPs; an over-broad fix (global lock, lock on every request, resetting the IP counter on success) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: unknown username (must lock out the same way so lockout does not reveal account existence; fix.diff:421-425)
many usernames from one IP (per-IP limit; fix.diff:414-418)
one username from many IPs (per-username limit; fix.diff:398-404)
username longer than 64 chars (truncated key; fix.diff:221-223, fix.diff:244-245)
client behind trusted reverse proxy vs spoofed X-Forwarded-For from an untrusted peer (fix.diff:495-515)

O7_producer.where: src/aniworld/web/app.py:283-285 (waitress serve options decide what request.remote_addr holds; the fix adds _proxy_options at fix.diff:77-93)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A self-service 'change my password' endpoint next to the admin user API that re-verifies the current password through db.verify_user without the throttle.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The user-management API block already lives here and has no password-change route; a maintainer adding one would naturally reuse verify_user and forget the throttle that lives only in login().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An HTTP Basic auth branch in _from_request/authenticate that accepts username:password for scripted /api/ access and calls db.verify_user directly.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This function already parses Authorization: Bearer; adding Basic for curl users is a common request, and it sits in a different module from the login throttle.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The debug app.run path (and any second server path) not receiving the proxy options, so a planted alternative server bootstrap keys the throttle on the proxy IP.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix only wires _proxy_options into waitress.serve; a second serve path is already present at this line.

O9_family: Authentication: missing brute-force / failed-login rate limiting (CWE-307), with a side fix for username-enumeration timing (CWE-208)

O10_build.toolchain: pip install -e .[test] (setuptools, pytest); Flask, flask-wtf, waitress, werkzeug
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_auth.py (local login, setup, logout via Flask test client using auth_client/admin fixtures), tests/test_db_users.py (verify_user, SSO accounts); the fix adds tests/test_login_throttle.py

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an in-memory per-IP failure counter in login() keyed on request.remote_addr (or X-Forwarded-For), with no per-username limit, no lockout for unknown usernames and no trusted-proxy handling.

out_of_scope_notes: db.verify_user at src/aniworld/web/db.py:269 skips hashing for unknown usernames (timing-based username enumeration); the same fix closes it, but it is a different CWE.
API keys at src/aniworld/web/apikeys.py:64 have no failure throttle, but the key is 32 random bytes (src/aniworld/web/apikeys.py:31-32), so brute force does not apply; not counted as an O8 route.
